title: The Editors’ Table
paragraphs: At a table covered with draft pages, a group of young editors discussed their next publication. Each person had brought a different account. Rather than rank the experiences from best to worst, they decided to explore the connections among them and preserve the details that mattered.

The first section of the collection placed these observations side by side. The witness continued to assert that she had seen the missing car. A diagram may clarify the instructions and make them easier to follow. The principal will commend the students for their honesty. Passengers began to complain about the long delay.

A later section added further scenes for comparison. After seeing the evidence, he had to concede that his theory was wrong. She chose to confide her worries to a trusted friend. The new measurements contradict the claim that the room is square. The council will debate the benefits and costs of the new park.

When the group returned to its original question, the discussion had become more precise. The members could point to particular actions and details instead of relying on a vague impression. They did not force every account to teach the same lesson. Their final display invited readers to compare the evidence, explain a connection, and consider where that connection ended.

targets.definition: to make something easier to understand
to admit something after initially resisting
to tell someone a private matter in trust
to say the opposite of a statement
to discuss opposing views of an issue
